label: miso 35 zonal refinement
definition: MISO 35: 6-zone zonal refinement (phase 1 of the zonal-refinement scope) — Midwest split to the six measured EIA-930 sub-BA/LRZ-union zones (West/Plains/Illinois/Indiana/East/South) with per-season hourly CIL/CEL deliverability caps from the LOLE Study Reports and the RDT one-way pair (3,000/2,500 MW) attached to Plains (D3: no spurious Plains congestion; kept). One-way link bounds newly wired (the RDT had been silently symmetric). STRUCTURAL GATES: (1) interfaces bind — RDT N-to-S 71/326/1074 h and S-to-N 3077/2033/877 h (23/24/25); West CIL 701/232/672 h; Illinois CEL 1199/541/984 h; (2) zonal prices separate — hours with spread >$1 go 0 to 2519/1467/717 (max spread $20-28) — but zone MEAN LMPs stay nearly flat and South sits ~$0.4-1.1 below Midwest (S-to-N exports of cheap South CCGT; mean-level sign check needs the D6 per-hub LMP upload to score); (3) Illinois shows near-zero local scarcity as expected; East/South import-at-limit in scarcity hours cannot fire with the scarcity tail still at 0 h — reserve co-opt deliberately OFF this run (phase 2 re-enables it, gate 4). Same offer stack as the miso-31 keeper; level metrics essentially unchanged (2025 coal +10.4% vs +10.5%; C3a -8.5/-13.7/-17.0%). Most structurally faithful MISO run.
